newsitem.title: USA: Big B seen bowing to buyer.
newsitem.headline: Big B seen bowing to buyer.

text.p: Revco D.S. Inc is unlikely to give up on tender-target Big B Inc now that the drugstore group has rejected its $15 a share offer and opened itself to other possible bidders.
CVS, Eckerd and Rite Aid are among likely buyers for Big B, a 389-outlet company centered in the South that is widely considered ripe for takeover, said analyst Napoleon Overton of Morgan Keegan.
"(Revco co-chairman) Sam Zell is an aggressive guy and is unlikely to give up very easily," Overton said.
Spokesmen for Revco, operator of more than 2,100 drugstores, were not available to comment.
Revco already owns 5.4 percent of Big B, the nation's 10th largest drugstore chain in a rapidly consolidating sector and its cash tender announced two weeks ago was valued at about $330 million.
Big B's stores, including those in the highly desirable Atlanta market, dovetail well with Revco's existing networks of outlets, analyst said.

"See Revco raising offer (and) competing offers likely, but think number two drugstore intent on buying Big B as part of an aggressive acquisition strategy," said the Standard & Poor's Marketscope investment-advisory service.

Overton said Rite-Aid, with some 2,800 drug stores, was likely eyeing Big B's commanding presence in Atlanta. Rite-Aid is entering that market and could jump quickly to profitability there with Big B's stores, Overton said.
"The only ones in any shape, both financially and geographically, likely to be white knights are Rite-Aid, Eckerd or CVS," said an analyst who requested anonymity.
A spokesmen for Eckerd declined to comment, while spokeswomen for CVS, a unit of Melville Corp, were not immediately available.

JP Morgan analyst Mark Husson said Revco's offer had already been raised $1 from the $14 proposed in private bargaining earlier this year and was towards the high end of valuations in other recent industry deals.
"The $15 bid was 47 percent of sales, which is at the top end of these things. Most got at 39-42 percent of sales," Husson said.
Big B shares closed up 5/8 at 16-7/8, a level analysts said reflected market sentiment that a higher offer was coming after Big B's announcement it was turning down Revco's offer.
